title: Probing Nanoscale Vibrational Properties in Monoclinic Beta Gallium Oxide via Vibrational EELS
content: With the advent of combined scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) instruments capable of sub-Ångstrom spatial and single meV energy resolution, many new possibilities are now available for understanding quasiparticle behavior towards the atomic scale. These advances have typically only been demonstrated on high symmetry or two-dimensional materials, allowing for easier interpretation of spectroscopic data. In particular, our understanding of phonons and their behavior has been transformed by these new experimental techniques, including the ability to detect modes resulting from single atomic defects [1]. Phonons control many properties of crystals, such as thermal and electronic transport, making them vital to our understanding of semiconductor behavior.
